content.text: sweep github open PRs, oldest to newest, and look for duplicates, overlap and opportunities to consolidate and/or group into clusters. beware of gh and bd commands that automatically apply limits to results, making it look like there are less items than there are.
quota limit approaching, lean on codex. your role is orchestration.
Understood — I'll orchestrate and push the analysis work to Codex scouts. First, let me pull the full open-PR list to disk (one cheap gh call with an explicit high limit so nothing gets truncated).

input.command: gh pr list --repo gastownhall/beads --state open --limit 1000 --json number,title,author,createdAt,updatedAt,headRefName,labels,isDraft,mergeable,additions,deletions,changedFiles > /tmp/claude-1000/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd/50a1f1f4-5639-400a-ad1e-00224fa105a6/scratchpad/open-prs.json && jq length /tmp/claude-1000/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd/50a1f1f4-5639-400a-ad1e-00224fa105a6/scratchpad/open-prs.json
input.description: Fetch all open PRs from gastownhall/beads to scratchpad

input.command: cd /tmp/claude-1000/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd/50a1f1f4-5639-400a-ad1e-00224fa105a6/scratchpad && for n in $(jq -r '.[].number' open-prs.json); do gh pr view $n --repo gastownhall/beads --json number,files -q '{number: .number, files: [.files[].path]}' 2>/dev/null; done > pr-files.jsonl; wc -l pr-files.jsonl
input.description: Fetch changed-file lists for all 104 open PRs

input.command:
cd /tmp/claude-1000/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd/50a1f1f4-5639-400a-ad1e-00224fa105a6/scratchpad && jq -s --slurpfile meta open-prs.json '
  (map({(.number|tostring): .files}) | add) as $f |
  $meta[0] | sort_by(.createdAt) | map({
    number, title, author: .author.login, createdAt, updatedAt,
    mergeable, isDraft, changedFiles,
    labels: [.labels[].name],
    files: ($f[(.number|tostring)] // [])
  })' pr-files.jsonl > pr-merged.json && jq length pr-merged.json && du -h pr-merged.json
input.description: Merge PR metadata with file lists, sorted oldest first

input.command:
scripts/codex-agent reviewer -o /tmp/claude-1000/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd/50a1f1f4-5639-400a-ad1e-00224fa105a6/scratchpad/cluster-report.md "You are analyzing the open PR queue of gastownhall/beads for a maintainer. Read the file /tmp/claude-1000/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd/50a1f1f4-5639-400a-ad1e-00224fa105a6/scratchpad/pr-merged.json — an array of all 104 open PRs sorted oldest to newest, each with: number, title, author, createdAt, updatedAt, mergeable (MERGEABLE/CONFLICTING/UNKNOWN), isDraft, changedFiles count, labels, and the list of changed file paths.

Task: sweep oldest to newest and identify:
1. DUPLICATES — PRs solving the same problem (same or near-same files + same intent from titles). List each duplicate set with PR numbers, and which one looks canonical (prefer newer/mergeable/smaller unless title suggests otherwise).
2. OVERLAP — PRs that touch the same subsystem/files enough that merging one will conflict or partially obsolete others. Build these as named clusters (e.g. by subsystem: sync/dolt, CLI commands, server mode, docs, CI, etc.).
3. CONSOLIDATION opportunities — groups that could be reviewed/merged as one batch (same author with related PRs, stacked/dependent-looking branches, mechanical same-shape changes across many PRs).
4. SINGLETONS — PRs touching files nothing else touches (safe to review independently).

Output a well-structured Markdown report: summary stats up top (total, drafts, conflicting count, cluster count), then a section per finding category. For every cluster give: cluster name, PR list as one line each ('#NNNN (author, age, mergeable-state, N files): title'), shared files/subsystem, and a one-sentence recommended action. Be exhaustive — every one of the 104 PRs must appear in exactly one primary cluster or the singletons list; include a final coverage check stating the count adds to 104. Compute ages relative to today 2026-07-27." </dev/null; echo "exit=$?"
input.description: Run Codex reviewer to cluster 104 open PRs
